items.title: Scientists first directly measure upper-atmosphere pollution from SpaceX rocket reentry

featured_image.name: SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets are grounded after inflight break up

items.description:
For the first time, researchers have directly measured pollution in Earth's upper atmosphere from a specific piece of space debris, tracing a plume of lithium vapor back to the uncontrolled reentry of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket over Europe last year.

The findings, published Thursday in the journal Communications Earth & Environment, mark a milestone in understanding how the burgeoning commercial space industry may be altering atmospheric chemistry in ways scientists are only beginning to comprehend.[1][2]

items.title: US deploys largest Middle East air force since 2003 Iraq invasion

featured_image.name: F-35s Deploy Closer to Middle East After US Talks with Iran

items.description:
The United States is assembling the largest concentration of military air power in the Middle East since the 2003 invasion of Iraq, positioning dozens of advanced fighter jets and a second aircraft carrier to the region as President Donald Trump weighs potential strikes on Iran.

According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, the U.S. Air Force has moved F-35s, F-22 Raptors, F-15Es, and F-16s to Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan and Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia in recent days, based on flight-tracking data. Command-and-control aircraft essential for large air campaigns, including E-3 Airborne Warning and Control System and E-11 Battlefield Airborne Communications Node aircraft, are also inbound.[1][2][3]

items.title: Climate change adding 47 extra days of harmful heat in coffee regions

featured_image.name: What climate change means for the future of coffee, cashews ...

items.description:
The world's leading coffee-producing regions are facing an average of 47 additional days of harmful heat annually due to climate change, threatening global harvests and contributing to elevated consumer prices, according to a new analysis released Wednesday by Climate Central.[1][2]

The study examined daily temperatures from 2021 to 2025 across 25 countries that represent 97% of global coffee production. Every country analyzed experienced more coffee-harming heat than would have occurred without fossil fuel pollution.[2][1]

items.title: South Korea's ex-president Yoon sentenced to life for insurrection

featured_image.name: South Korea's former President Yoon sentenced to five years: What we know

items.description:
Former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol was sentenced to life in prison on Thursday after a court found him guilty of leading an insurrection through his ill-fated declaration of martial law in December 2024, ending one of the most dramatic political crises in the country's democratic history.

Presiding Judge Ji Gwi-yeon of the Seoul Central District Court ruled that Yoon "directly and proactively planned" the insurrection and acted "with the purpose of subverting the Constitution by sending the military to the National Assembly to paralyze or limit its function for a substantial amount of time." Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that Yoon bore primary responsibility for destabilizing the constitutional order and had shown no remorse.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump convenes Board of Peace as Gaza disarmament stalls

featured_image.name: Trump convenes first 'Board of Peace' meeting as Gaza ...

items.description:
US President Donald Trump presided over the first meeting of his Board of Peace on Thursday, convening representatives from more than 45 nations in Washington to discuss the reconstruction of Gaza and the deployment of an international peacekeeping force. The meeting, held at the renamed Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace, comes as the Israel-Hamas ceasefire remains fragile and the central challenge of disarming Hamas unresolved.[1][2]

Trump announced this week that participating nations have pledged $5 billion for humanitarian relief and reconstruction efforts in Gaza, alongside commitments to deploy thousands of personnel to an International Stabilization Force aimed at maintaining security as Israeli forces withdraw from the territory.[3][4][5]

items.title: UK study finds space-based solar could compete by 2040

featured_image.name: Japan Aims to Beam Solar Power From Space in Groundbreaking First

items.description:
Space-based solar power could become cost-competitive with traditional energy sources by 2040, according to a new UK government-commissioned feasibility study released this month. The report arrives as international momentum builds toward orbital solar demonstrations this year, potentially transforming a concept once relegated to science fiction into a practical energy solution for an increasingly power-hungry world.

The study, conducted by Frazer-Nash Consultancy, projects that the levelized cost of electricity from small-scale orbital solar plants could drop from between GBP 0.0335 and GBP 0.0595 per kilowatt-hour in 2030 to between GBP 0.0087 and GBP 0.0129 per kilowatt-hour by 2040. At those prices, space solar would be competitive with nuclear and tidal power technologies. The study found that launch costs, projected to fall to approximately GBP 550 per kilogram by 2040 in an optimistic scenario, are the most significant cost driver, accounting for more than 50% of variance in electricity costs.[1]

items.title: Repsol aims to boost Venezuela oil output 50% after U.S. lifts sanctions

featured_image.name: Sueldo de Josu Jon Imaz en Repsol 2025: ¿Cuánto ganó el CEO?

items.description:
Spanish energy giant Repsol disclosed Thursday that Venezuela owes it €4.55 billion ($5.37 billion), while simultaneously announcing ambitious plans to boost oil production in the South American nation by more than 50 percent within the next year following the United States' reauthorization of operations there.

The debt revelation came in Repsol's annual 2025 financial report, which shows the company is owed for commercial debt tied to oil and gas supplies, late payment interest, and €947 million in financing for its Petroquiriquire joint venture with Venezuela's state-owned PDVSA. Repsol has provisioned around €3.59 billion for these receivables over the years.[1][2]

items.title: Former Prince Andrew arrested over Epstein files allegations

featured_image.name: UK ex-Prince Andrew arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public ...

items.description:
Thames Valley Police arrested Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly Prince Andrew, on Thursday morning on suspicion of misconduct in public office, marking the first time in contemporary history that a senior royal has been taken into custody.

Officers in plain clothes arrived at Wood Farm on the royal Sandringham Estate in Norfolk around 8 a.m. local time and detained the 66-year-old on his birthday, according to BBC and ITV reports. Police confirmed they are conducting searches at properties in Berkshire and Norfolk as part of the investigation.[1][2][3]

"As part of investigation, we have today arrested a man in his sixties from Norfolk on suspicion of misconduct in public office," Thames Valley Police said in a statement. In accordance with national guidelines, police declined to name the arrested individual, though multiple British outlets confirmed it was the king's younger brother.[4][1]

items.title: Study finds oxygen-using ancestors, solving complex life mystery

featured_image.name: Ancient microbes may have used oxygen 500 million years ...

items.description:
Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin have resolved a fundamental puzzle about how animals, plants, and fungi evolved, publishing findings in the journal Nature that show our ancient microbial ancestors could use oxygen, contrary to what scientists had long believed.

The discovery addresses a paradox that has troubled evolutionary biologists for years. The prevailing theory holds that all complex life, called eukaryotes, arose when two very different microbes merged billions of years ago. One of these ancestral microbes, the alphaproteobacterium that became the mitochondria, required oxygen to survive. The other, an Asgard archaeon, was thought to live exclusively in oxygen-free environments. How these two organisms came into close contact remained unexplained.

items.title: European stocks dip as oil surges on U.S.-Iran tensions

featured_image.name: Uncertainty around Iran leads to choppy oil prices

items.description:
European markets pulled back slightly Thursday after hitting record highs a day earlier, as investors weighed surging oil prices against escalating tensions between the United States and Iran over Tehran's nuclear program.

The pan-European Stoxx Europe 600 Index dipped 0.1% in early trading, settling around 628 points after reaching an all-time high on Wednesday. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 fell 0.3%, while Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 each declined around 0.2% to 0.3%.[1][2][3]
